name: Residential Streetscapes of Seoul in 360° (SP-Scheme)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (65 new Google Street View 360° panoramas of residential streets in Seoul). This is the paper's web-based evaluation: after giving gender and age, each participant gets 15 randomly drawn 360° street views in random order, drags each view with the mouse or finger to look left, right, up and down, and rates it on 10 evaluation items (comfort, friendliness, harmony, naturalness, beauty, regularity, personality, cleanliness, artificiality, safety) and overall satisfaction, each on the paper's 5-point scale (1 strongly disagree, 2 somewhat disagree, 3 neutral, 4 somewhat agree, 5 strongly agree). The paper compares these web ratings with the same images seen in a VR headset and models overall satisfaction from the 10 items with multi-level ordered logistic regression.

Original study: Han & Lee (2023), Land 12(2), 345. 375 GSV panoramas randomly sampled from residential areas of Seoul (GSV taken 2009–2021 at 20 m intervals on the road network), 30 graduate students of urban planning (25 analysed), 15 panoramas each, web evaluation in August 2021 followed by the same images in VR.

Differences from the original study: (1) 65 panoramas from random points across Seoul, kept by eye when they showed residential streets (the paper used residential zoning to sample 375); captured 2009–2018, mostly 2018; (2) only the web-based evaluation, not the VR session; (3) the item wording is written for this template as agree statements ("This streetscape feels comfortable.", "Overall, I am satisfied with this residential streetscape.") because the paper names the items but does not print the statements; (4) the paper also collected address for identification; this template asks only gender and age. Images: © Google Street View.
author: Han, J., & Lee, S.

.item.miss>b{color:#b3261e}
